environmental.altitude: no performance degradation up to 15000 ft (4572 m)
environmental.operating-temp: -40 to 60 C in a sealed enclosure, -40 to 70 C in a ventilated enclosure (40 LFM) and -40 to 75 C in a blower-equipped enclosure (200 LFM), up to 15000 ft; safety certified at 60 C
environmental.storage-temp: -40 to 85 C in the shipping container

features.dry-contact-alarm: two alarm inputs (5 V threshold) and one alarm relay output (NO, COM, NC), Table 4
features.macsec: the four uplink ports are MACsec capable
features.optics-sfp: the 24 front cages take 1 Gbps SFP transceivers; Tables 49 and 50 list the industrial-grade 1 G optics against the ambient they allow. The supported list is in Juniper's Hardware Compatibility Tool, which the guide names and which is not held here
features.optics-sfp-plus: the eight group cages take 1 Gbps SFP and 10 Gbps SFP+ transceivers; Tables 45 to 48 list the industrial-grade 10 G and 10GBASE-T optics against the ambient they allow. The supported list is in Juniper's Hardware Compatibility Tool, which the guide names and which is not held here
features.virtual-chassis: up to 10 EX4100, EX4100-F and EX4100-H switches; the four VCP cages are the Virtual Chassis ports (HiGig or HGoE mode, or uplink ports) and the four uplink cages support HGoE only. A 10GBASE-T transceiver cannot form a Virtual Chassis in a VCP

physical.weight: 8.07 kg (17.79 lb) with no supply; 9.20 kg with one AC supply and 9.23 kg with one DC supply, Table 13

power.power-input-dc: 20.4 through 72 VDC at the terminal block, nominal +24, -48 or -60 VDC (Table 36)

thermal.cooling: fanless, convection cooled (Table 12); one rack unit clear above and below

gaps.note: Table 12 lists a 90 W AC and a 90 W DC FRU supply for the one model EX4100-H-24F and the packing list (Table 67) says the supply is "AC or DC", specific to the SKU, but the guide names no switch part number for the DC build. The DC build is drawn as an example configuration and is not exported as a device type.

alarm.note: Table 4 and Figure 22 - the dry contact connector (callout 15) is a six-pole plug on a 3.5 mm pitch at 195.2 mm across and 26.9 mm down, with GND, IN 0, IN 1, NO, COM and NC printed at 45 degrees over it, each with a tick to its pole. The alarm input threshold is 5 V and the plug is preassembled (Table 67).

chassis.note: Tables 13 and 14 - height 1.7 in (4.33 cm), width 17.28 in (43.90 cm), depth 14.96 in (37.99 cm), weight 17.79 lb (8.07 kg) with no supply, 20.28 lb (9.20 kg) with one AC supply and 20.24 lb (9.23 kg) with one DC supply. The inch and centimetre figures of the height disagree by 0.2 mm (1.7 in is 43.18 mm); the centimetre figure, 43.3 mm, is used. Unlike the EX4100-H-24MP, the guide gives one depth for both supplies. The width is the body between the bracket fold lines: the guide says the front mounting brackets extend it to 19 in (Table 56), and the figures show no ears.

colour.note: The face colour is the photograph's median of the bare front and rear, #6a727f, which Figure 5 agrees with.

drawing-vs-photo.note: The legends are drawn from Figure 5 and the photograph, which agree: the model line reads EX4100-H 24F in light grey (the figure prints it dark, as it prints every legend), and there is no orange frame or orange numeral on a model with no PoE. The maker's logo and Mist AI mark are not drawn and are reserved as a logo-zone. Figure 6 draws a DC supply in the first slot where the photograph shows an AC one; the outlines are the same and both supplies are modelled.

ears.note: Table 7 and the mounting topics (Figures 67 to 79) - two-post rack mounting is the default, with the EX4100-H-2P-RMK kit provided in the box: a pair of side brackets that hang on shoulder screws and slide toward the rear, with M4 by 6 mm screws, mounting the switch flush with the front posts. The orderable four-post kits are EX4100-H-4P-RMK (screws, with rear mounting blades) and EX4100-H-4P-TL-RMK (toolless rails). No position other than flush is stated and none is measured. No kit contract is written: the guide gives no rack-depth range, preset or rail depth for any of the three kits (Table 56 states only a 27 in minimum cabinet depth, which is a cabinet figure and not a kit range), and a kit configuration needs one of the two, so a contract would carry an invented range. The kits stay in provenance only. The guide asks for 1 RU clear above and below.

earthing.note: Table 68 and Figure 100 - a two-hole protective earthing terminal on the rear panel for a Panduit LCD6-14A-L lug on two M5 by 10 mm screws with washers (the grounding kit is JNP-GL-2H6-M5-RA, separately orderable). The figure shows two holes 15.9 mm apart (the 5/8 in lug pitch) on a lighter plate at the right end. They are drawn as holes on the plate; the library has no pair part for M5 holes on that pitch, so no lug seat is offered.

management.note: Figure 5 - the management Ethernet port (MGMT, callout 4, with its two lamps), the USB 2.0 Type-A host port (callout 12) and the RJ-45 RS232 console port (CON, callout 13) are stacked in one metal housing 14.4 mm wide, upside down for the management port as the keyway shows. The housing is too narrow for the full RJ-45 jack and holds ganged cells, 12.7 by 11.0. The USB Type-C console port (callout 2, CON), the RESET pinhole (callout 3) and the round Mode button (callout 14, the Factory Reset/Mode button) are in a row to the left of it. The claim code label (callout 9) is a sticker.

port-lamps.note: Figures 14, 16 and 18 and Table 19 - every cage has a Link Activity lamp and a Status lamp: two round lamps beside the cage's number, above the upper row and below the lower row. The Status lamp shows what the mode lamps select (Table 20), so its states cannot be one vocabulary here.

port-numbering.note: Figure 5 and the photograph - the legends over the upper row read 0, 2, 4 and on to 22 and under the lower row 1, 3 and on to 23, so the upper cage of a column is the even port. The cage groups print 0 and 2 over the upper row and 1 and 3 under the lower row, with the group's name, VCP or UPLINK, over it. The numbers are as printed, from 0. Interface names are not printed on the metal, and the guide's factory-default configuration is for the 12MP, so none is recorded.

ports.note: Table 13 and Figure 5 - 24 SFP cages in two rows in two banks of six columns: ports 0 to 11 from 10.0 mm across and ports 12 to 23 from 103.1 mm. The columns are on a 14.7 mm step, not the registry's 14.25, which is the cage's width and leaves no gap; the cages are the registry's 14.25 mm wide and are placed on the measured step. The rows are 14.3 mm apart, upper cell at 9.2 mm and lower at 23.5, the upper row turned 180 as in a stacked cage. Then two groups of four SFP/SFP+ cages, each two columns by two rows: the Virtual Chassis ports (callout 11, VCP) and the uplink ports (callout 7, UPLINK), with rows 12.6 mm apart.

power.note: Tables 12, 25, 28 and 35 - 90 W AC or DC supplies, 100 to 240 VAC and 20.4 to 72 VDC. The guide gives no PoE budget (there is no PoE) and no maximum input power for the chassis.

power-input.note: Figure 5, callout 10, and the connection steps - behind a terminal door at the right of the front, two sections, PSU 0 and PSU 1, each with six terminals: L, N and G above and DC+, DC- and G below, the AC row over an AC symbol and the DC row under a DC symbol. The terminals of a section serve the supply in the rear slot of the same number. The door has a Phillips screw at its right end and the legends are printed inside it. The guide asks for an external 2-pole or 4-pole circuit breaker rated 20 A minimum for AC and a 2-pole 25 A, 80 VDC breaker for DC. Torque and tool belong to provenance only.

power-modules.note: Table 12, Tables 25, 28, 35 and 42, Figure 6 and the removal and installation topics - the two supply slots take JPSU-H-90W-AC (90 W AC) and EX4100-H-24F-DC-PSU (90 W DC), field-replaceable and hot swappable, N+1 redundant, in any combination of one or two. The switch ships with one preassembled (Table 67) and the guide describes a blank on the second slot (callout 2 of Figure 6). The guide gives no airflow direction: the switch is fanless and convection cooled, so there is no airflow variant, and the handle colour on the photograph is green. The supplies are components in the bays.

rear.note: Figure 6 and the photograph - from the left, the serial number label, the supply in slot 0 with its retaining thumbscrew on a tab at the left end, a bracket with a second screw, the slot 1 blank with a captive screw at each end, then the ESD point (callout 3), the physical security lock slot (callout 5) with its padlock mark and the earthing plate (callout 4) with its symbol. PSU 0 is printed above the first tab and PSU 1 at the right end of the blank. This is the reverse of the EX4100-H-24MP's rear, which has the earthing plate, ESD point and lock slot at the left.

scale.note: Gate 1 - Figure 5 is 3000 px wide; the body outline is 2883.5 px across, 6.568 px/mm against 439.0 mm, and 284.5 px high, 6.57 px/mm against 43.3 mm: 0.1 percent apart, so it is orthographic and carries geometry. Figure 6 (the rear) is 2860 px across and 283 px high: its aspect, 10.1, agrees with the table's 10.14 to 0.5 percent, but its body reads 3.3 mm short of 439.0 at the front's scale, so the figure is drawn about 0.8 percent small. Positions from the left of the rear figure are taken at the front's scale; those right of the blank are measured from the right edge of the figure and carried 3.3 mm so that they sit from the right edge of the 439.0 mm body. The photographs (2100 px wide, 4.17 px/mm) agree with the figures to about a millimetre. Every position is estimated, good to about 0.3 mm across and 0.2 down on the front and 0.6 across on the rear.

sources.note: EX4100-H Switch Hardware Guide, Juniper Networks (copyright Hewlett Packard Enterprise Development LP), published 2026-10-01, 299 pages, https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/hardware/ex4100-h/ex4100-h.pdf (sha256 recorded under references): Tables 3 to 8, 12 to 15, 16 to 22, 25, 28, 32, 35, 36 and 42, Figures 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 26, 30 and 32, the mounting topics (Figures 67 to 79), the power connection steps and the packing list (Table 67). The guide's flat front and rear figures (Figures 5 and 6, 3000 px wide) are the pictures measured. Juniper's studio photographs of the model, front and rear (2100 px wide), from the maker's public image library (https://www.juniper.net/content/dam/www/assets/images/us/en/image-library/ex-series/ex4100-h-24f/ex4100-h-24f-front-high.jpg and ex4100-h-24f-rear-high.jpg), confirm the colours, the lamps, what is printed and the seated supply; neither is copied here. The EX4100 datasheet (https://www.juniper.net/content/dam/www/assets/datasheets/us/en/switches/ex4100-line-of-ethernet-switches-datasheet.pdf) redirects to an HPE PSNow document that did not answer, so no datasheet figure is used. No Visio stencil or 3D model of the EX4100-H was found. Nothing is taken from a reseller. End of life was searched 2026-10-23 and no Juniper notice for the EX4100-H was found, so the lifecycle is none announced.

status-block.note: Figures 5, 8 and 20 and Tables 16 and 20 - two columns of lamps: the chassis lamps SYS, ALM, MST and CLD at 265.5 mm across and the port mode lamps SPD, DX and EN at 271.4 mm (the PoE lamp is not fitted to a model without PoE ports, the note under Figure 19), each legend over its lamp and each lamp 7.1 mm below the one above. The three dry contact alarm lamps (IN 0, IN 1 and OUT, Tables 21 and 22) are at 259.5 mm with a bell mark and the legend over each, and the PSU 0 and PSU 1 lamps at 341.5 mm beside the cage groups. The lamps are round, 2.4 mm across in the figure; common/led-dot@1 is 2.0 and is used.
